thread:
ingrid: seeing repeated OOMs on prod inference hosts tied to kv cache growth for long-context sessions. stack traces point to kv allocator, not GPU OOM. paging spikes before crash.
ingrid: root cause looks like fragmentation + reuse failure when many long-history chats hit different prefixes.
alex: can you paste the perf dump? curious about live_kv_bytes and allocation counts.
ingrid: pasted profiler snippet from the failing host: ```
KV_STATS: live_entries=183421 live_kv_bytes=12.3GB total_allocs=1.9M free_fragments=2432
PAGE_EVENTS: swapped_pages=1123 peak_page_latency_ms=132
BATCH_PROFILE: avg_tokens=18 batch_wait_ms=4
```
maria: that live_kv_bytes / free_fragments ratio screams fragmentation. allocator is leaving many small holes.
ken: did we recently change kernel selection or attention tiling? small-chunk kernels can increase per-head KV footprints.
ingrid: we shipped a kernel selector tweak last week to favor tiled matmul for throughput on A100s. rollout was partial.
perf-bot: perf-alert: +22% kv memory growth observed in canary after kernel-selector-v3 rollout (compare baseline last 7d).
alex: ok. two mitigations to try: 1) force compaction sweep when free_fragments > threshold; 2) enable LRU eviction by session age for long contexts.
maria: also consider immediate fallback when kernel selector produces higher kv-per-token — routing policy can pick compact-kernel model variant.
dana: can we do a safe runtime mitigation: cap kv retention per-session to N bytes and stream older prefix to disk (paging) with async prefetch?
sre: paging to disk helped in staging but increased tail latency. we need graceful degradation: return partial history + 206 style response rather than fully blocking.
ken: for quick mitigation I can add a background compaction job that coalesces free fragments every 30s and a soft cap that triggers LRU eviction of least-recently-used KEYs. low-risk rollout behind flag.
ingrid: please also add metrics: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_evictions_by_policy, kv_paged_bytes so we can alert earlier.
alex: small config patch to batching heuristics might reduce memory pressure: reduce max_contiguous_batch to 8 for sessions > 1024 tokens so caches are reused more.
maria: adding a test harness that simulates 10k concurrent long-context chats with random prefix variations would help reproduce fragmentation. I can wire that into perf lab.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/kv-compact-sweep -> canary (3 hosts) by ken, ETA 10m.
sre: monitoring note: if we see page latency > 100ms or evictions > 50/s, auto-scale fallback to dedicated-instance tier for affected customers.
dana: also adding retry/backoff for callers: if kv allocation fails, return 429 with Retry-After + minimal output; avoid immediate retry storms.
alex: longer-term: evaluate KV offload to host DRAM with a compacted layout and optional compression (int8/quantized keys), or NVMe-backed KV with async eviction. both require kernel and runtime work.
ingrid: for postmortem, collect per-session allocation traces and shard-level fragmentation maps. I'm grabbing heapdumps on next crash.
ken: rolling the compaction flag now to canary. will keep it off for very-high-throughput routes until we measure latency impact.
maria: thanks — after canary let's run the synthetic long-context harness for 30m and compare kv_fragmentation_ratio and peak_page_latency.
ingrid: ack. will also add a playbook entry: when OOM suspected from KV, first flip compaction, limit session kv cap, then route to compact-kernel variant, finally escalate to dedicated fallback.
perf-bot: noted: created ticket PERF-1428 for fragmentation + kernel-selector interaction.
ken: update: canary deployed, compaction job running at 30s interval. initial memory delta: -420MB per host after sweep. will monitor.
sre: nice. if we get stable numbers we'll stage a wider rollout with auto-trigger heuristics. :thumbsup:
